steps.title: Before you come
steps.lead: Choosing a hospital is step one, not step zero.
steps.body: Pick a few, send inquiries, compare what comes back. Ask about the medical visa early — which one you need depends on what you are having done.
steps.askEn: Have you done this procedure before? Roughly how many days will all of it take?
steps.askKo: 이 시술을 해 본 적이 있나요? 전부 며칠쯤 걸리나요?

steps.title: Getting here
steps.lead: Arrival, and the trip from the airport to the hospital.
steps.body: Ask who meets you and in what language. This is arranged by the hospital, not by us.
steps.askEn: Who meets me at the airport? Will an interpreter be there?
steps.askKo: 공항에서 누가 맞아 주나요? 통역이 붙나요?

steps.title: First visit
steps.lead: This is where the price becomes real.
steps.body: Examination, consultation, then a treatment plan with a cost attached. Anything quoted before this is an estimate.
steps.askEn: What is not included in this price?
steps.askKo: 이 금액에 안 들어간 것은 무엇인가요?

steps.title: Treatment
steps.lead: The procedure and any hospital stay.
steps.body: Consent should happen in a language you actually read. If you are handed a Korean form and no translation, stop and ask.
steps.askEn: Can I read the consent form in my own language?
steps.askKo: 동의서를 제 언어로 볼 수 있나요?

steps.title: Recovery here
steps.lead: You usually stay in Korea for a while after treatment.
steps.body: How long is a medical decision, not a travel one — ask before you book the flight home.
steps.askEn: When am I allowed to fly?

steps.title: After you go home
steps.lead: The part people worry about most.
steps.body: Who do you contact if something goes wrong six time zones away? And will your own doctor be able to read your records?
steps.askEn: Will you send my records to my doctor at home?
steps.askKo: 진료 기록을 제 나라 의사에게 보내 주나요?
